title: The Road Runs Like a River
text: The thaw has turned the road to the village into a river of mud.

choices.label: Send the boys with stones
choices.chronicle: {When}, the boys laid stones across the worst of the road, and the carts came through again by Sunday.

choices.label: Let the road wait for the sun
choices.chronicle: {When}, the road was left to the sun, and the village walked the long way round by the bog.

title: Weevils in the Flour
text: The flour from the last delivery is full of weevils, and the bread smells of them.

choices.label: Sift it and bake it anyway
choices.chronicle: {When}, the flour was sifted through a cloth, and the bread was eaten without asking what was in it.

choices.label: Throw the whole sack out
choices.chronicle: {When}, the sack was thrown on the midden, and the house went a day with less bread.

title: Tallow, Not Wax
text: The candle-maker has come up from the village with a pot of tallow instead of wax.

choices.label: Buy the tallow
choices.chronicle: {When}, the tallow was bought, and the chapel smelled of mutton all winter.

choices.label: Use the tallow in the kitchen and keep the wax
choices.chronicle: {When}, the tallow went to the kitchen, and the chapel was lit with the old wax, and the old brothers muttered.

title: The Snoring Brother
text: One brother's snoring has kept the dormitory awake for a month.

choices.label: Move him to the guesthouse
choices.chronicle: {When}, the snoring brother was moved to the guesthouse, and the dormitory slept, and the guesthouse did not.

choices.label: Let them sleep in the chapel
choices.chronicle: {When}, the dormitory slept in the chapel by the fire, and the snoring went on alone.

title: Swallows in the Bell-Tower
text: A pair of swallows has built a nest in the bell-tower, over the rope.

choices.label: Leave them be
choices.chronicle: {When}, the swallows were left in the bell-tower, and the brothers said they were a sign of spring.

choices.label: Knock the nest down
choices.chronicle: {When}, the nest was knocked down, and the swallows went away over the bog and did not come back that year.

title: Turnips Gone in the Night
text: Turnips have been dug up in the night from the top field.

choices.label: Set a watch on the field
choices.chronicle: {When}, a watch was set on the top field, and a brother sat out in the cold for three nights.

choices.label: Blame the village boys
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house blamed the village boys, and the village did not forget who had said it.

title: Wet Winter Wood
text: The woodshed roof has let the rain in on the winter's wood.

choices.label: Dry it by the kitchen fire
choices.chronicle: {When}, the wood was dried by the kitchen fire, and the kitchen had warmth for a week and a little extra bread.

choices.label: Burn it damp and see
choices.chronicle: {When}, the damp wood was burned, and the smoke was bad, and two brothers coughed through the hall for days.

title: A Cough at the Gate
text: A pilgrim has come to the gate with a bad cough and asks for a bed in the guesthouse.

choices.label: Give him a bed and the medicine
choices.chronicle: {When}, the pilgrim was given a bed and the medicine, and left at dawn with a blessing and a new cough he would not talk about.

choices.label: Send him on to the village
choices.chronicle: {When}, the pilgrim was sent down to the village, and the village had to take him in.

title: A Map of the Bog Road
text: A traveller shows a map of the bog road that is better than the house's own.

choices.label: Buy the map with bread
choices.chronicle: {When}, the map was bought for bread, and copied into the scriptorium's book of roads.

choices.label: Copy it in the scriptorium
choices.chronicle: {When}, the map was copied quickly and carelessly, and the copy was no better than the house's own.

title: The Eel Weir
text: The eel weir at the river mouth is full, but the fishermen say the house has no right to it.

choices.label: Share the catch
choices.chronicle: {When}, the catch was shared with the fishermen, and they said grace over the eels with the brothers.

choices.label: Keep the weir
choices.chronicle: {When}, the weir was kept, and the fishermen went home grumbling along the shore.

title: A Carter in the Snow
text: Snow has blocked the gate, and a carter is stuck outside with a load of salt.

choices.label: Dig him out
choices.chronicle: {When}, the brothers dug the carter out, and he gave them a sack of salt for their trouble.

choices.label: Wait for the thaw
choices.chronicle: {When}, the carter waited three days in the snow, and the salt was ruined by the wet.

title: Three Pages Missing
text: Three pages of the hymnal are missing from the lectern book.

choices.label: Copy them again
choices.chronicle: {When}, three pages were copied again from the chapter house book, and the lectern had its hymns.

choices.label: Sing from memory
choices.chronicle: {When}, the hymns were sung from memory, and the missing pages were not missed by anyone but the copyist.

title: The Lame Goat
text: The goat that gives the milk has gone lame in the hind leg.

choices.label: Set the leg with splints
choices.chronicle: {When}, the leg was set with splints, and the goat walked again, and gave a little milk.

choices.label: Slaughter her for the pot
choices.chronicle: {When}, the goat went to the pot, and the children asked where the milk had gone.

title: A Boy Asks for Letters
text: A boy of twelve has come to the gate and asks whether he may be taught his letters.

choices.label: Take him in to be taught
choices.chronicle: {When}, the boy was taken in to learn his letters, and he learned the alphabet before the frost.

choices.label: Send him home with a leaf of the psalter
choices.chronicle: {When}, the boy went home with a leaf of the psalter, and his mother cried at the door.

title: The Night Drill
text: The abbot orders a fire drill at night, and the brothers complain bitterly about it.

choices.label: Keep the drill
choices.chronicle: {When}, the drill was kept, and the house ran out into the cold in its shirts, and grumbled all the way back to bed.

choices.label: Cancel it
choices.chronicle: {When}, the drill was cancelled, and the brothers slept, and the buckets stayed by the well where no one would find them in the dark.

title: Salt for a Rule
text: A merchant offers a sack of salt for a copy of the Rule.

choices.label: Trade the copy for salt
choices.chronicle: {When}, a copy of the Rule went down the road for salt, and the merchant swore the house had made a good bargain.

choices.label: Refuse him
choices.chronicle: {When}, the merchant was refused, and went off down the road with his salt unsold.

title: An Oak from the Bog
text: Men from the bog have dug up a great oak trunk and offer it for the house's timber.

choices.label: Take it for firewood
choices.chronicle: {When}, the oak was cut and stacked, and it burned slowly through the winter with the bog smell in it.

choices.label: Refuse it
choices.chronicle: {When}, the oak was refused, and the men from the bog took it away to sell in the town.

title: The Sheet Torn Loose
text: A storm has torn a sheet of lead from the chapel roof, and it hangs by a nail.

choices.label: Pull it back with ropes
choices.chronicle: {When}, the lead was pulled back with ropes in the wind, and the brothers sang the whole time to keep their hands steady.

choices.label: Patch it with tarred cloth
choices.chronicle: {When}, the roof was patched with tarred cloth, and the patch held until the spring.

title: The Cracked Barrel
text: The rain barrel by the kitchen door has cracked along one stave.

choices.label: Mend it with pitch
choices.chronicle: {When}, the barrel was mended with pitch and went back to catching the rain.

choices.label: Set a bucket under the crack
choices.chronicle: {When}, a bucket was set under the crack, and the kitchen grumbled at every drip.

title: Bells on the Water
text: A sea mist has come in, and the fishermen say they hear bells out on the water.

choices.label: Ring the chapel bell for them
choices.chronicle: {When}, the chapel bell was rung for the fishermen through the mist, and the boats came home by it.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house ignored the bells on the water, and the fishermen said they would not forget who had stayed silent.

title: The Secretary's Visit
text: A bishop's secretary wants to see the house's accounts, all of them.

choices.label: Show him every account
choices.chronicle: {When}, every account was shown to the secretary, and he wrote in his book that the house had nothing to hide.

choices.label: Show him only the good pages
choices.chronicle: {When}, only the good pages were shown, and the secretary knew it, and wrote that down too.

title: The Raven and the Racks
text: A raven steals the bread crumbs from the drying racks, one by one, while the kitchen watches.

choices.label: Set a net over the racks
choices.chronicle: {When}, a net was set over the racks, and the raven was caught and let go again beyond the wall.

choices.label: Let the bird have its share
choices.chronicle: {When}, the raven was given its share, and the kitchen laughed at it all week.

title: The Night in the Woods
text: A young brother has been missing in the woods for a night and a day.

choices.label: Send two men to search
choices.chronicle: {When}, two men went into the woods with torches, and found the brother at dawn, asleep under a holly tree, with a bird in his hands.

choices.label: Pray for him and wait
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house prayed and waited, and the brother came back at noon, cold and frightened, and wept at the gate.

title: Someone at the Wine
text: Someone has been at the sacramental wine in the sacristy, and the jar is half empty.

choices.label: Ask the kitchen boys
choices.chronicle: {When}, the kitchen boys were questioned one by one, and each swore on the psalter that he had not touched it.

choices.label: Say nothing and buy more
choices.chronicle: {When}, the jar was filled again from the cellar, and no one asked who had drunk the first half.
